name: Editorial Authority
tagline: A broadsheet front page for independent human rights research
idea: Daybreak’s homepage is composed like the front page of a quality newspaper: a centred nameplate, one dominant lead story, a dated Latest column and dense supporting coverage, all set on a twelve-column grid with fine column rules.
fit: Daybreak’s credibility rests on evidence. A newspaper’s visual language signals rigour, independence and timeliness, helps journalists and policymakers scan quickly, and gives research, news and calls to act a clear, trusted order.
informedBy: A strong editorial lead with clear scanning hierarchy, favouring asymmetry over equal cards
A dated, typed stream of the latest news for a sense of recency
Hierarchy carried by scale, spacing and rules rather than decorative containers
distinct: The only concept built on newspaper conventions: a nameplate masthead, column rules, a dated Latest column, drop caps and ruled boxes. It is the densest, most text-led of the ten.
buttons: Square-cornered: crimson solid for giving and actions, ink outline for reading, underlined slate text links, and uppercase hairline-boxed topic tags.
imageDirection: Natural colour, documentary-style images in 3:2 crops, always with a visible caption and credit. One dominant lead image; smaller pictures sit in disciplined rows beneath hairline rules.
navigation: Centred nameplate flanked by date and Donate; sections between double rules. Mobile: compact masthead, sideways-scrolling section bar.
visualCharacter: Broadsheet newspaper: serif, ruled, dense and authoritative
contentEmphasis: Lead investigation, latest news and research publications
bestFor: An organisation whose reputation rests on credible, frequently published research and news for informed audiences.
tradeoffs: Dense and text-heavy: it needs a steady flow of strong content and photography, and feels less warm than story-led concepts.
